title: FIDIC Contracts Management: Practical Use of FIDIC Contracts
overview: This course offers practical insights for professionals involved in the management or administration of projects governed by FIDIC forms of contracts. It focuses on the essential procedures and disciplines required in both the “Pre-Contract” phase, including the FIDIC Client Consultant Service Agreement and selecting the appropriate FIDIC contract form, as well as the “Post-Contract” phase, addressing contract management and claim-related issues.

The course covers the use of FIDIC’s 1999 Contracts while highlighting key updates in the 2017 Second Editions. Participants will gain a deep understanding of FIDIC’s conditions of contract for construction (“Construction Contract”) and plant and design-build (“Design-Build Contract”). This knowledge ensures confidence in working with these contracts, whether as employers, consultants, or contractors.
audience: This course is ideal for professionals from government agencies, private employers, consulting engineers, contractors, quantity surveyors, architects, legal advisers, funding agencies, insurers, and anyone involved with FIDIC contracts.
methodology: The course is interactive, featuring group discussions, case studies, and syndicate work. Practical exercises are integrated to allow participants to apply their advanced knowledge and demonstrate their skills in managing FIDIC contracts effectively.
objectivesIntro: By the end of the course, participants will be able to:
objectives: Select the most suitable FIDIC form of contract for various projects.
Apply FIDIC principles, mechanisms, and best practices in contract and project management.
Understand the responsibilities, obligations, and entitlements of employers and contractors.
Define the engineer’s roles, duties, and responsibilities under FIDIC contracts.
Implement FIDIC-compliant mechanisms for payments, claims, and dispute resolution.
